event.description:

? Admission: $13.00 includes Skate Rental

✨ Non-Skating Parents: $4.00

✨ STAR 1 | Marchers

  • Beginner Non-Rollers
  • Body Posture
  • Proper Way to Fall
  • Proper Way to Get Up
  • Stand with Feet in a V
  • March in Place
  • March While Moving
  • Coast on 2 Feet

  • Forward Scissors
  • Stop with Tow Stop
  • Cannon Ball in Place
  • Cannon Ball Rolling
  • Balance on 1 Foot Standing

  • Balance on 1 Foot Rolling
  • Backward Walk
  • Backward Scissors
  • Backward Stopping
  • 2 Ft. Jump Standing
  • 2 Ft/ Jump Rolling
  • Cannon Ball Rolling
  • Shoot the Duck

✨ STAR 4 | Rollers

  • Explaining All Edges
  • Learn to Press Edge on 1 Ft Outside & Inside Forward
  • Forward Crossovers Standing
  • Forward Crossovers Rolling
  • Roll on 1 foot Across Floor with Leg in Front & then in Back
  • Balance on 1 foot Backwards
  • Scooter Pushes
  • 1 foot Jump

event.title: WORKSHOP: FOUND FAMILIES
event.description:
@

WORKSHOP
FOUND FAMILIES
Saturday, October 17th | 1:00pm – 4:00pm
$45

REGISTER

This collage workshop with Artist-in-Residence Eli Craven focuses on re-interpreting family image archives through alterations and combinations with additional found and made materials. We explore family photography and portraiture, the meanings they carry, and how we can transform them through these added materials. You may use additional materials such as thread, fabric, papers, documents, wood, mirrors, metals, etc. As we create collages and tell stories, we will also discuss the meaning behind the combinations of these materials and how images change over time.

You are encouraged to bring some of your own materials to work with: copies and test strips, in addition to originals of photographs intended to use in the workshop. A variety of found photographic images and various sources will also be available.

Partial scholarships available by request to info@surelsplace.org.

BIOGRAPHY

Although currently based in Indiana, Eli Craven was raised in Idaho. “Returning to Idaho for this project feels appropriate given the origins of my relationship to photography and a return to the subject matter of my childhood,” Eli says. In his childhood home, magazines and movies were censored, select films and TV shows were forbidden, sexuality and death were seldom discussed. The power images hold was discovered through scrutinizing forbidden magazine collections, daytime soap operas, and movies. The impetus of his practice resides in this desire to see, only to discover nothing shocking. Instead, seemingly mundane imagery is isolated and fragmented, presenting a narrative exploring the image’s role in processes of socialization.

Eli left Idaho with a BFA in photography from Boise State back in 2011. He went on to pursue an MFA in photography at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. Currently an Associate Professor of Photography at Purdue University, his work has been widely exhibited and published. Most recently his work has been exhibited at Kant Gallery in Copenhagen, Denmark; KlompChing Gallery in Brooklyn, New York; and at the Blue Sky, Oregon Center for the Photographic Arts in Portland, Oregon.

EXHIBIT & ART TALK
A PLEA FOR TENDERNESS
Thursday, October 29th | 7:00pm – 8:30pm
free

In this project Eli Craven aims to position the viewer as a collaborator or partner in the physical experience of the work. Viewers are invited to alter photographic compositions through a series of kinetic elements and reflective materials, including sliding wood panels, hinged doors, and movable peepholes. The viewer must engage and activate the framing components to reveal the photographic image, potentially provoking the desire to see what is hidden within. Participation is integral to this project, with entire scenes rendered incomplete without the viewer’s touch and imagination filling the gaps and visualizing what lies beneath the surface of the photograph, or behind the veil.

Although the works exist within the canon of photography, they are sculptural objects that utilize the photograph as part of their construction. Eli’s work started with an obsession for photography and its materials and that fixation remains at the core of his practice.

event.title: Statewide Grief Support Group
event.description:
We most often think of grief as a response to the death of someone close. It is that, but it is more. For caregivers, it is something that is continuous, daily, often lasting for years before the passing of the one for whom they’re providing care. In the emotionally jumbled, stressful experience of being a caregiver, who listens and understands? Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska does, and we are
offering a place and time for caregivers to be heard, to share thoughts and feelings, and find solace. Join us.

We offer compassionate grief support groups on the first and third Thursdays of each month, led with care by Gay Wellman through Zoom. We welcome anyone navigating the loss of a loved one, as well as caregivers and others who continue to experience anticipatory grief due to Alzheimer’s disease or another form of dementia.

Because the groups meet online, people from communities across the state can come together to share stories, receive understanding, and find comfort in the company of others who truly get what they are going through. Whether your grief is fresh or something you have carried for a while, you will find a place here where your feelings are honored and you do not have to face them alone.

You are welcome just as you are.

With questions or to sign up, reach out to Gay Wellman at gwellman@alzalaska.org.

event.title: Savvy Caregiver: October 1 – November 5
event.description:
This online class is for family members caring for a loved one with Alzheimer’s disease or related dementia. The class meets for weekly on Thursdays for six-weeks from October 1st – November 5th from 1:00-3:00. The focus is on improving the practice of caregiving. There is a thorough overview of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementia as well as the emotions the caregiver may face, a tool for decision making, and how to deal effectively with family issues. You will learn about the stages and how to use that to help your loved one stay “in the Zone.”

This course provides:

  • Information on ADRD.
  • Knowledge of how dementia affects the person.
  • Ideas for setting up daily care and activities for success.
  • Strategies for figuring out what behaviors mean and how to respond.
  • Tools for decision-making.

This class takes place on Zoom.

To help Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska cover licensing and provider costs, there is a fee for participation. Classes are $140 and pre-registration is required. This fee includes access to all 6 weeks of the course including all educational materials. Financial assistance is available.  Education materials may be picked up in Anchorage or Mat Su or mailed throughout Alaska.

For more information  and to register contact Janice Downing: jdowning@alzalaska.org or 907-864-3408

Space is limited – sign up today!

Come and share the joy of Art Links with us via Zoom on the first Tuesday of every month!

Art Links is a welcoming program for adults who want to have fun, meet new people, and keep their minds active and creative. If you are worried about your memory, a care partner, a person experiencing brain changes, or at risk of social isolation, Art Links is a great way to enjoy art, poetry, music, and meaningful connection in a relaxed, friendly setting. Through a variety of creative activities, Art Links encourages self expression, socialization, and connection. Participants may enjoy:

  • A variety of artistic mediums
  • Poetry, music, and movement
  • Memory rich conversations
  • Creative activities facilitated by ARA staff and local artists

Art Links is free and open to all abilities. No registration is required. Friends and family are welcome to join! For more information, contact Janice Downing at jdowning@alzalaska.org or 907-864-3408.

event.title: Mind Sharpener (Mind Aerobics)
event.description:
Your brain deserves a workout just as much as your body does. Mind Sharpener is a fun, interactive program designed to keep your mind active, flexible, and strong.

This program is perfect for anyone looking to maintain or improve cognitive wellness, stay mentally active, and enjoy the benefits of a stronger, sharper brain. Held on Mondays and Fridays over the course of 12 engaging sessions, you’ll participate in exercises proven to boost six essential areas of cognitive function:

  • Memory – techniques to retain and recall information more effectively
  • Concentration – strategies to sharpen focus and attention
  • Processing Speed – exercises to think and respond more quickly
  • Visual-Spatial Acuity – strengthen awareness and orientation skills
  • Language – build word-finding, comprehension, and communication abilities
  • Problem Solving – practice creative and logical thinking approaches
  • Plus, you’ll enjoy a bonus session exploring ways to continue building brain health long after the program ends.

📌 Registration is required. Email Debbie Chulick at dchulick@alzalaska.org to get registered and for more information.

💲 Cost: $140 to cover materials and provider costs. Financial assistance is available – please reach out if cost is a concern.

event.title: CG101: What Is Lewy Body Dementia?
event.description:
October is Lewy Body Dementia Awareness Month, making it an important time to learn more about this complex and often misunderstood form of dementia.

Join Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska for CG101: What Is Lewy Body Dementia?, an educational class designed to help caregivers, family members, and community members better understand Lewy body dementia. Participants will learn about common signs and symptoms, how Lewy body dementia may differ from other forms of dementia, and what caregivers may experience as the disease progresses. event.title: Statewide Grief Support Group
event.description:
We most often think of grief as a response to the death of someone close. It is that, but it is more. For caregivers, it issomething that is continuous, daily, often lasting for years before the passing of the one for whom they’re providing care. In the emotionally jumbled, stressful experience of being a caregiver, who listens and understands? Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska does, and we are
offering a place and time for caregivers to be heard, to share thoughts and feelings, and find solace. Join us.

We offer compassionate grief support groups on the first and third Thursdays of each month, led with care by Gay Wellman through Zoom. We welcome anyone navigating the loss of a loved one, as well as caregivers and others who continue to experience anticipatory grief due to Alzheimer’s disease or another form of dementia.

Because the groups meet online, people from communities across the state can come together to share stories, receive understanding, and find comfort in the company of others who truly get what they are going through. Whether your grief is fresh or something you have carried for a while, you will find a place here where your feelings are honored and you do not have to face them alone.

You are welcome just as you are.

With questions or to sign up, reach out to Gay Wellman at gwellman@alzalaska.org.

event.title: The Page Turners Book Club: Aging with Grace
event.description:
The Page Turners Book Club: Aging with Grace

Join us for our NEW Page Turners Book Club, a welcoming monthly discussion group for anyone interested in brain health, healthy aging, and lifelong learning. Caregiving can be demanding, and it’s easy to put your own interests aside. This book club is an opportunity to slow down, enjoy a good book, and connect with others who understand the caregiving journey. Read at your own pace, then join us each month to share insights, discuss the reading, celebrate successes, talk through challenges, and support one another in a welcoming, judgment free environment.

REGISTER HERE! 

Our first featured book is Aging with Grace by Dr. David Snowdon, the groundbreaking account of the landmark Nun Study, one of the most influential studies on aging and Alzheimer’s disease. Together, we’ll explore what this remarkable research teaches us about cognitive health, resilience, purpose, and the factors that may help support brain health throughout life.

The club meets on the 4th Wednesday of each month from 6:00 to 7:30 p.m., beginning August 26, and is open to participants in Fairbanks and statewide via Zoom.

For our first discussion in August, we’ll cover Chapters 1 through 3. During our September meeting, we’ll discuss 4-6, in October we’ll discuss chapters 7-9, and we’ll close out the book in November with chapters 10-13. We’ll begin a new book club in January with Tangled but Sarah Leavitt – stay tuned for more.

event.title: Mind Sharpener (Mind Aerobics)
event.description:
Your brain deserves a workout just as much as your body does. Mind Sharpener is a fun, interactive program designed to keep your mind active, flexible, and strong.

This program is perfect for anyone looking to maintain or improve cognitive wellness, stay mentally active, and enjoy the benefits of a stronger, sharper brain. Held on Mondays and Fridays over the course of 12 engaging sessions, you’ll participate in exercises proven to boost six essential areas of cognitive function:

  • Memory – techniques to retain and recall information more effectively
  • Concentration – strategies to sharpen focus and attention
  • Processing Speed – exercises to think and respond more quickly
  • Visual-Spatial Acuity – strengthen awareness and orientation skills
  • Language – build word-finding, comprehension, and communication abilities
  • Problem Solving – practice creative and logical thinking approaches
  • Plus, you’ll enjoy a bonus session exploring ways to continue building brain health long after the program ends.

📌 Registration is required. Email Debbie Chulick at dchulick@alzalaska.org to get registered and for more information.

💲 Cost: $140 to cover materials and provider costs. Financial assistance is available – please reach out if cost is a concern.

event.description:

Join Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska and Debbie, who will be hosting this CG101 class focused on making the holiday season and travel more comfortable, meaningful, and safe for everyone. We will discuss ways to adapt holiday traditions, prepare family and friends for visits, reduce overstimulation, and create celebrations that include and support a loved one living with dementia.

New to caregiving? CG101 is a great place to start. This class series provides practical information and tools to help you better understand dementia, navigate changing needs, establish supportive routines, and care with confidence.

event.title: Caregiver 101: Healthy Body, Healthy Brain
event.description:
Taking care of your brain is an important part of taking care of your overall health. As we grow older, maintaining both mental sharpness and physical vitality can play an important role in supporting independence, connection, and quality of life.

Join Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska for CG101: Healthy Body, Healthy Brain, a free, engaging 60 minute program presented in collaboration with the Alzheimer’s Association. This class explores current research and practical strategies for supporting lifelong brain health through everyday choices and habits.

Participants will learn about the connections between brain and body health, including the role of nutrition, physical activity, cognitive engagement, and social connection. The class will also offer practical ideas for incorporating healthy habits into daily life and making positive changes at any age.

Whether you are a caregiver, concerned about your own brain health, supporting someone you love, or simply interested in healthy aging, this class provides useful information and approachable ways to support both your body and your brain.

event.title: Statewide Grief Support Group
event.description:
We most often think of grief as a response to the death of someone close. It is that, but it is more. For caregivers, it is something that is continuous, daily, often lasting for years before the passing of the one for whom they’re providing care. In the emotionally jumbled, stressful experience of being a caregiver, who listens and understands? Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska does, and we are
offering a place and time for caregivers to be heard, to share thoughts and feelings, and find solace. Join us.

We offer compassionate grief support groups on the first and third Thursdays of each month, led with care by Gay Wellman through Zoom. We welcome anyone navigating the loss of a loved one, as well as caregivers and others who continue to experience anticipatory grief due to Alzheimer’s disease or another form of dementia.

Because the groups meet online, people from communities across the state can come together to share stories, receive understanding, and find comfort in the company of others who truly get what they are going through. Whether your grief is fresh or something you have carried for a while, you will find a place here where your feelings are honored and you do not have to face them alone.

You are welcome just as you are.

With questions or to sign up, reach out to Gay Wellman at gwellman@alzalaska.org.

event.title: Caregiving 101: Money Conversations
event.description:
Talking about money can be difficult for any family, and dementia can make those conversations even more important. Planning ahead can help families better understand their options, make informed decisions, and reduce uncertainty as needs change over time.

Join Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska for CG101: Money Conversations, a practical class focused on navigating financial discussions related to aging, dementia, and caregiving. Participants will learn about the importance of starting conversations early, identifying financial information and responsibilities, planning for future care needs, and involving the right people in the decision making process.

This class will also explore strategies for approaching sensitive financial conversations with respect and compassion, recognizing potential financial concerns, and taking steps to help protect a loved one’s wishes and financial well being.

Whether you are new to caregiving, helping a family member plan for the future, or simply want to be better prepared, this class offers a helpful starting point for conversations that can sometimes feel difficult to begin.

New to caregiving? CG101 is a great place to start. This class series provides practical information, tools, and resources to help you better understand dementia, navigate changing needs, and care with confidence.

event.title: The Page Turners Book Club: Aging with Grace
event.description:
The Page Turners Book Club: Aging with Grace

Join us for our NEW Page Turners Book Club, a welcoming monthly discussion group for anyone interested in brain health, healthy aging, and lifelong learning. Caregiving can be demanding, and it’s easy to put your own interests aside. This book club is an opportunity to slow down, enjoy a good book, and connect with others who understand the caregiving journey. Read at your own pace, then join us each month to share insights, discuss the reading, celebrate successes, talk through challenges, and support one another in a welcoming, judgment free environment.

REGISTER HERE! 

Our first featured book is Aging with Grace by Dr. David Snowdon, the groundbreaking account of the landmark Nun Study, one of the most influential studies on aging and Alzheimer’s disease. Together, we’ll explore what this remarkable research teaches us about cognitive health, resilience, purpose, and the factors that may help support brain health throughout life.

The club meets on the 4th Wednesday of each month from 6:00 to 7:30 p.m., beginning August 26, and is open to participants in Fairbanks and statewide via Zoom.

For our first discussion in August, we’ll cover Chapters 1 through 3. During our September meeting, we’ll discuss 4-6, in October we’ll discuss chapters 7-9, and we’ll close out the book in November with chapters 10-13. We’ll begin a new book club in January with Tangled but Sarah Leavitt – stay tuned for more.

Books are available through Amazon, ThriftBooks, Kindle, and other online retailers. You may also be able to borrow the ebook or audiobook through the Libby app with your local library card or check with the Noel Wien Library or your local library for available copies.

Whether you’re a caregiver, healthcare professional, or simply interested in healthy aging and brain health, we invite you to read, reflect, and connect with us. We look forward to learning and growing together.

Register today via Zoom.

event.title: Statewide Grief Support Group
event.description:
We most often think of grief as a response to the death of someone close. It is that, but it is more. For caregivers, it is something that is continuous, daily, often lasting for years before the passing of the one for whom they’re providing care. In the emotionally jumbled, stressful experience of being a caregiver, who listens and understands? Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska does, and we are
offering a place and time for caregivers to be heard, to share thoughts and feelings, and find solace. Join us.

We offer compassionate grief support groups on the first and third Thursdays of each month, led with care by Gay Wellman through Zoom. We welcome anyone navigating the loss of a loved one, as well as caregivers and others who continue to experience anticipatory grief due to Alzheimer’s disease or another form of dementia.

Because the groups meet online, people from communities across the state can come together to share stories, receive understanding, and find comfort in the company of others who truly get what they are going through. Whether your grief is fresh or something you have carried for a while, you will find a place here where your feelings are honored and you do not have to face them alone.

You are welcome just as you are.

With questions or to sign up, reach out to Gay Wellman at gwellman@alzalaska.org.

event.title: Statewide Grief Support Group
event.description:
We most often think of grief as a response to the death of someone close. It is that, but it is more. For caregivers, it issomething that is continuous, daily, often lasting for years before the passing of the one for whom they’re providing care. In the emotionally jumbled, stressful experience of being a caregiver, who listens and understands? Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska does, and we are
offering a place and time for caregivers to be heard, to share thoughts and feelings, and find solace. Join us.

We offer compassionate grief support groups on the first and third Thursdays of each month, led with care by Gay Wellman through Zoom. We welcome anyone navigating the loss of a loved one, as well as caregivers and others who continue to experience anticipatory grief due to Alzheimer’s disease or another form of dementia.

Because the groups meet online, people from communities across the state can come together to share stories, receive understanding, and find comfort in the company of others who truly get what they are going through. Whether your grief is fresh or something you have carried for a while, you will find a place here where your feelings are honored and you do not have to face them alone.

You are welcome just as you are.

With questions or to sign up, reach out to Gay Wellman at gwellman@alzalaska.org.

event.title: Art Links – Fairbanks (in-person)
event.description:
Come and share the joy of Art Links with us in Fairbanks! Art Links is a social support program that promotes engagement for individuals diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias or seniors at risk of isolation and depression. By using a variety of creative art ideas, we promote self-expression as well as socialization and meaningful connections. Participants enjoy:

  • A variety of artistic mediums
  • Music and movement
  • Memory-rich conversations
  • Facilitated by ARA staff and local artists.

Free to attend! No registration required. Share with friends and family. With questions, contact Jennifer Willeford at JWilleford@alzalaska.org or 907-621-6071.

event.title: Statewide Caregiver Support Group: Virtual
event.description:
Caregiving can be both deeply meaningful and incredibly challenging. It is common to feel rewarded and overwhelmed at the same time. You may sometimes feel like no one truly understands what you are going through, but you are not alone. We understand, and support is available.

Caregiver Support Groups bring together people with shared experiences to offer encouragement, understanding, and practical insight. These groups provide emotional and social support, a chance to learn what has worked for others, and information about helpful local resources.

Free to attend, this is an online support meeting available statewide in Alaska on the second and fourth Thursday of each month. You may join by phone or Zoom and attend one meeting or continue coming as often as you find helpful.

event.title: Statewide Grief Support Group
event.description:
We most often think of grief as a response to the death of someone close. It is that, but it is more. For caregivers, it is something that is continuous, daily, often lasting for years before the passing of the one for whom they’re providing care. In the emotionally jumbled, stressful experience of being a caregiver, who listens and understands? Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska does, and we are
offering a place and time for caregivers to be heard, to share thoughts and feelings, and find solace. Join us.

We offer compassionate grief support groups on the first and third Thursdays of each month, led with care by Gay Wellman through Zoom. We welcome anyone navigating the loss of a loved one, as well as caregivers and others who continue to experience anticipatory grief due to Alzheimer’s disease or another form of dementia.

Because the groups meet online, people from communities across the state can come together to share stories, receive understanding, and find comfort in the company of others who truly get what they are going through. Whether your grief is fresh or something you have carried for a while, you will find a place here where your feelings are honored and you do not have to face them alone.

You are welcome just as you are.

With questions or to sign up, reach out to Gay Wellman at gwellman@alzalaska.org.

event.title: Statewide Grief Support Group
event.description:
We most often think of grief as a response to the death of someone close. It is that, but it is more. For caregivers, it is something that is continuous, daily, often lasting for years before the passing of the one for whom they’re providing care. In the emotionally jumbled, stressful experience of being a caregiver, who listens and understands? Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska does, and we are
offering a place and time for caregivers to be heard, to share thoughts and feelings, and find solace. Join us.

We offer compassionate grief support groups on the first and third Thursdays of each month, led with care by Gay Wellman through Zoom. We welcome anyone navigating the loss of a loved one, as well as caregivers and others who continue to experience anticipatory grief due to Alzheimer’s disease or another form of dementia.

Because the groups meet online, people from communities across the state can come together to share stories, receive understanding, and find comfort in the company of others who truly get what they are going through. Whether your grief is fresh or something you have carried for a while, you will find a place here where your feelings are honored and you do not have to face them alone.

You are welcome just as you are.

With questions or to sign up, reach out to Gay Wellman at gwellman@alzalaska.org.

The chrysanthemum takes center stage once again at Luthy Botanical Garden for a beloved Peoria fall tradition! event.title: Zootober
event.description:
Halloween gets a little WILD at Zootober! Each weekend, Peoria Zoo comes alive with glowing lights, creepy creatures, surprising characters, and plenty of Halloween fun for the whole family.

Explore the Zoo as you make your way through immersive Halloween scenes featuring lifelike animatronics, dazzling light displays, and live actors waiting around the corner. Stroll along spooky trails and displays while collecting candy at stops along the way. Grab a spooky snack or themed drink, stop for a Halloween photo op, enjoy hands-on activities, and see what strange new creatures you might encounter.

Event hours: 5:30 – 9:00 PM
Last ticket sales: 8:00 PM

Ticket Information:
Tickets can be purchased online or in-person at the Zoo or Noble Center
Online Sales: $14 / person (includes any online fees)
In-Person Sales: $17 / person
Members: Get 10% off with discount code!
Tickets are required for guests ages 2 and up
Zootober uses timed entry tickets at 5:30, 6:00, 6:30, 7:00, 7:30, and 8:00 p.m. Your ticketed time is simply your entry window. Once you’re inside, you’re welcome to stay and enjoy Zootober until the event closes!

Please note, all ticket purchases are final. There will be no animals on exhibit during Zootober, but the Zoo will be crawling with eerie “creatures”!

Click here for more information about the event, including Saturday night entertainment, Wildly Accessible Day, Glen Oak Express train schedule and more!

 

Whether you’re looking for Halloween thrills, a night of family fun, or just an excuse to put on a costume and wander through the Zoo after dark, Zootober is ready to get a little spooky.

event.title: The Fungus Among Us
event.description:
There is a Fungus Among Us! Join our Naturalists as we discover the fantastic world of fungus. We will go for a hike in the Nature Preserve to see what Mushroom Mischief is a foot!

Members: FREE

Non-members: $5

Please register for this program. All ages welcome.

event.title: Peoria PlayHouse: Fall Maker Crafternoons
event.description:
Come make with us and get creative this fall!

Take inspiration from the colors, textures, and changes of the season during Fall Crafternoons at the Peoria PlayHouse Children’s Museum! Families are invited to explore their creativity and make something all their own using recycled and repurposed materials from the Maker Space.

Create a seasonal decoration, experiment with different materials, or simply make something fun to take home. There’s no right or wrong way to create — bring your imagination and see where it takes you!

Fall Crafternoons are designed for the whole family to create, explore, and enjoy making together.

Ages 5-12
$12 for members | $14 for non-members

Each crafter, including children and participating adults, should register individually.

Register Today!

event.title: Fright & Delight
event.description:
Get ready for an evening of spooky fun the whole family will love! Join us for Fright & Delight, Proctor’s biggest Halloween celebration, filled with candy, crafts, games, and glowing surprises.

Activities include:

  • Pumpkin Carving & Painting
  • Slime-Making & Face Painting
  • Glow-in-the-Dark Candy Hunt
  • Spooky Photo Booth
  • Trick-or-Treat Prize Wheel
  • Taste the Treats Challenge
  • Guess the Candy Jar Contest
  • Costume Catwalk Contest with prizes for Funniest, Scariest & Most Creative

Admission: $3 per person OR $12 per family (up to 5 people); admission is at the door.

Gather your costumes, bring your friends and family, and make memories at Fright & Delight: A Proctor Halloween Night!

event.title: Welcoming Walks: Women’s Halloween Hike
event.description:
Join us for a Women’s only trek and celebrate Halloween. Hike friendly costumes are encouraged. Connect with other adult women who like hiking, nature and meeting new people. There will be a short introduction and then we will be on our way. Prepare for hiking about 2 hours depending on breaks. This is a harder level hike with slopes. Bring water, snacks, appropriate hiking gear, layers, closed toed shoes etc.

This is an 18+ hike

Please register for this program.

Fees: FREE | Welcoming Walks are no cost. Donations are welcome.
